title: 科学技術と人・社会
subtitle: Science,Technology and Human Society
courseType: （Provided by all courses）Liberal Arts CoursesTransdisciplinary Learning
teachers: 授業科目の学習・教育目標
keywords: Science and technology and industry, nation, and policy
educationalGoal: In the 18th and 19th centuries, scientific activity was institutionalized and professionalized, becoming "science." In this course, we will review the relationship between science and technology, and between science-technology and human society. Interactions among science, technology, and human society led to the social and environmental issues being experienced now. Upon completing this course, students will be able to establish their own viewpoints as engineers and/or scientists who support society.

   science, the relationship between science and technology

   nations, economic development, and changing values
4. Social issues caused by science and technology:
   from environmental, information, and bioethics viewpoints
5. What is required for engineers and/or scientists in today's society?

lessons.content:
How science and technology work:
- Introduction to science and technology studies

Historical overviews on S&T 1:
From “natural philosophy” to “science”

Historical overviews on S&T 2:
Institutionalization and professionalization
of science

(cont.)
- Relationship between science, technology, and
industry

Interactions between science, technology,
and human society 1:
Modern nations, and science and technology

(cont.)
- War and science and society
- Case studies

Interactions between science, technology,
and human society 2:
Economic development, and science and technology

(cont.)
- Social distortion caused by economic growth
- Economic globalization

Interactions between science, technology,
and human society 3:
Changing values

Social issues caused by science and technology:
Environmental, information, and bio-ethics...

(cont.)
- Difference between information technology and
   other technologies
- Shift to an information-oriented society and
   issues caused by the shift

(cont.)
- Issues related to bioscience and biotechnology
- Social issues and SDGs

Wrap-up:
science and technology in and for human society
- What is required for scientists and/or
  engineers in today's society

Final reflection:
- Summary of this course
